slides.head_en: Creed in verse (1): the first lines
lines: أَبْدَأُ بِسْمِ اللهِ وَالرَّحْمَنِ * وَبِالرَّحِيمِ دَائِمِ الْإِحْسَانِ
I begin with the name of God, the Merciful, and with the Compassionate, constant in kindness.
فَاللهُ مَوْجُودٌ قَدِيمٌ بَاقِي * مُخَالِفٌ لِلْخَلْقِ بِالْإِطْلَاقِ
God exists, is without beginning, remains, and differs from creation in every way.
وَقَائِمٌ غَنِيٌّ وَوَاحِدٌ وَحَيّْ * قَادِرٌ مُرِيدٌ عَالِمٌ بِكُلِّ شَيّْ
He stands by Himself, is self-sufficient, One and Living, Able, Willing, Knowing everything.
فَقُدْرَةٌ إِرَادَةٌ سَمْعٌ بَصَرْ * حَيَاةٌ الْعِلْمُ كَلَامٌ اسْتَمَرّْ
Power, will, hearing, sight, life, knowledge, speech: they continue.
وَجَائِزٌ بِفَضْلِهِ وَعَدْلِهِ * تَرْكٌ لِكُلِّ مُمْكِنٍ كَفِعْلِهِ
And it is permissible for Him, by His favour and justice, to leave any possible thing as to do it.
وَالْمُسْتَحِيلُ ضِدُّ كُلِّ وَاجِبِ * فَاحْفَظْ لِخَمْسِينَ بِحُكْمٍ وَاجِبِ
And the impossible is the opposite of each obligatory attribute: so memorise fifty by an obligatory ruling.

lines: «الْوَاجِبُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ عَدَمُهُ،
"The obligatory": that whose non-existence cannot be conceived by the mind;
«الْمُسْتَحِيلُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ،

"the possible": that whose existence and non-existence can both be conceived by the mind.

lines: عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ: هُوَ عِلْمٌ يُعْرَفُ بِهِ إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْأَدِلَّةِ الْيَقِينِيَّةِ

"the impossible": that whose existence cannot be conceived by the mind;

sections.name: C
sections.en: A short text: the evening in the majlis. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَتْ أُخْتِي مَرْيَمُ مَعَ أُمِّنَا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
In the evening my sister Maryam sat with our mother in the majlis.
وَجَلَسْتُ أَنَا مَعَ عُمَرَ قُرْبَ الْبَابِ.
And I sat with Umar near the door.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ: هَلْ حَفِظْتِ الْعَقِيدَةَ؟
The Habib said to Maryam: Have you memorised the creed?
Maryam said: Yes, I have memorised it.
ثُمَّ فَتَحَتْ كِتَابَهَا وَقَرَأَتْ بَيْتًا بَعْدَ بَيْتٍ، وَالنَّاسُ جَالِسُونَ يَسْمَعُونَ.
Then she opened her book and read verse after verse, while the people sat listening.
وَكَانَ فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ، وَفِي آخِرِ النِّصْفَيْنِ قَافِيَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
And every verse had two halves, and at the end of the two halves one rhyme.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِي هَذِهِ الْعَقِيدَةِ صِفَاتُ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
The Habib said: In this creed are the attributes of God, and God is all-hearing, all-seeing.
وَسَأَلَ: مَا الْوَاجِبُ؟ وَمَا الْمُسْتَحِيلُ؟ وَمَا الْجَائِزُ؟
And he asked: What is the obligatory? What is the impossible? What is the possible?
قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ: اثْنَانِ وَاثْنَانِ أَرْبَعَةٌ، وَهَذَا وَاجِبٌ.
Maryam said: Two and two are four, and this is obligatory.
ثُمَّ دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ وَلِأُمِّهَا، وَرَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
Then the Habib prayed for Maryam and her mother, and we returned to the house, and praise be to God.

lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
